text:
incident-bot: 🚨 SEV2 detection: sudden spike in inference-prod errors in us-west-2. Pattern: repeated 'CUDA illegal memory access' on multiple pods (gpu-34, gpu-35). Auto-alert created.

alex kim: I'm seeing a cascade of OOM-ish failures, but logs show `illegal memory access` not straight OOM. Pulling kernel logs now.

mira shah: oncall here, taking primary. Alex can you paste the docker/kube logs?

alex kim: paste below — relevant excerpt:

```
2026-03-15T09:12:21Z inference-pod-12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
2026-03-15T09:12:22Z inference-pod-12 runtime: cuda: cudaErrorIllegalAddress at inference_runner.cc:412
2026-03-15T09:12:22Z inference-pod-12 containerd: container exited with code 139
```

alex kim: Also seeing these repeating on a subset of pods after a model swap earlier at ~09:00 (canary rollout).

sam choi: who triggered the canary? deploy-bot?

deploy-bot: @sam choi triggered rollout `model-v2.3 -> v2.4` at 2026-03-15T09:00:07Z. Canary 10% in us-west-2.

mira shah: ok possible correlation between model variant + kernel path. Workplan: cordon affected node(s), drain pods with `--grace-period=0` if crashing, rollback canary, and enable fallback routing to cpu-dyn for critical customers.

sre-lead: +1. Prioritise customer-impacted routes first (routes: /chat-stream, /completion-fast). Customer-success, please list customers on Dedicated clusters in us-west-2.

customer-success: Listing: AcmeRetail (dedicated), FinTracks (dedicated), small PLG accounts on hosted endpoints. AcmeRetail shows 5 min of increased 5xxs.

alex kim: kubectl describe node gpu-34: shows repeated PageWalk faults and sMMU errors: `pagewalk: non-canonical address`, also dmesg shows `misaligned address during page walk` bursts.

alex kim: quick commands I ran:
```
kubectl get pods -o wide | grep inference-prod
journalctl -k -u kubelet --since "10m"
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv
```

mira shah: Taking action now: cordon gpu-34 && drain with evict priority. Marking incident owner: mira shah.

ops-bot: Node gpu-34 cordoned by mira shah. Drain started.

alex kim: draining revealed pods restarting rapidly. Suggest immediate canary rollback to previous model v2.3 on us-west-2.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: model-v2.3 roll forward to 100% in us-west-2. ETA 2m.

sam choi: while rollback proceeds, set routing fallback: route `critical` customers to lowest-latency fallback model (v2.2-quant).

mira shah: done: routing rule added, critical routes now hitting fallback. Monitoring errors.

incident-bot: Error rate on /completion-fast dropped from 18% -> 6% after rollback and routing changes. Latency for fallback increased ~30ms.

alex kim: attaching heap trace snippet from the crashing container (sanitized):
```
#0 0x7f9d0123 in gpu_kern_exec()
#1 0x7f9d0456 in attention_forward()
#2 0x400abc in model_run()
#3 0x400def in worker_loop()
```

alex kim: Stack points at kernel-side mem access in an attention kernel. Could be a model-code-change exposing a rare race with the GPU driver.

sre-lead: escalate to eng-runtime and eng-ml. Tagging runtime oncall and kernel folks.

mira shah: handoff note for next shift: primary mitigation = rollback + node cordon; further triage required on kernel/driver mismatch + model binary layout. Customer-impact summary: AcmeRetail partial degradations for 6 minutes, no data loss. Severity remains SEV2 until full stabilization.

eng-runtime (via alex): quick hypothesis: new fused-kernel in v2.4 uses unaligned loads in corner-case sequence lengths causing DMA misalignment on certain driver versions. Repro steps being built.

sam choi: can we repro on a dev node with same driver and model binary? If yes, we can craft a minimal reproducer and test patch.

alex kim: spinning up a repro with model-v2.4 on matching AMI + driver 535.11. Temporary job id repro-451.

mira shah: handoff to @mira shah -> @mira shah (next oncall) in 45m. Leaving this thread with actionable checklist:
- rollback confirmed (done)
- cordoned nodes: gpu-34 (drained), gpu-35 (monitoring)
- fallback routing applied for critical customers
- contact list sent to eng-runtime and driver-team
- reproduce job initiated (repro-451)

customer-success: notifying AcmeRetail: short blip, rollback complete, we will follow up with RCA. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Rollback completed at 2026-03-15T09:07:14Z. Canary reverted.

mira shah: leaving detailed logs and a pointer to reproducer: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2678901234/repro-451.tar.gz. Next oncall please continue kernel/drivers bisect; if repro confirmed, schedule hotpatch or pin driver on affected pool.

alex kim: additional note: observed increased host OOM pressure just before the crashes — likely due to client traffic spike + KV cache growth. If kernel race exists, higher memory pressure might make it surface more often. Recommend increasing node memory headroom and enabling eviction thresholds.

sre-lead: create follow-up ticket: RUNTIME-5783 (kernel-race-investigation) and link to customer comms.

mira shah: signing off handoff: mira shah -> sam choi at 10:00 UTC. If sam is not available, notify @sre-lead.

sam choi: received, will pick up. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated (rollback + fallback) — monitoring for 1h. If error rate climbs back above 5% re-open.

mira shah: final comment before I leave: recommend blocklist model-v2.4 from us-west-2 until driver-compat confirmed. Also schedule post-mortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 PT with eng-runtime, eng-ml, infra, and customer-success.

customer-success: I'll prepare a short customer-facing note for AcmeRetail and FinTracks.

sre-lead: thanks everyone — good containment. Follow-up: triage, reproducer, driver bisect, and a comms update.

sam choi: picking up now.

ops-bot: Node gpu-34 uncordon scheduled in 2h if stable.
